items.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999
items.q: The transcript identifies Monk Rowe as the interviewer ('I’m very fortunate to have one of America’s great musicians, Phil Woods... I’m... Monk Rowe'). ctx.x: Saxophonist and composer Phil Woods is one of America’s most honored and respected jazz artists. He was born on November 2, 1931 in Springfield, Massachusetts and started on alto at the age of 12. He graduated from Juilliard as a clarinetist and was gigging with Kenny Dorham, Dizzy Gillespie and Quincy Jones by the mid-1950s. Phil has recorded prolifically for four decades, garnered numerous awards and penned notable compositions for small and large ensembles. While his playing reflects the influence of Benny…
Phil was interviewed in Delaware Water Gap, PA on November 8, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. We are in Delaware Water Gap at the Deer Head Inn and I’m very fortunate to have one of America’s great musicians, Phil Woods — clarinetist, saxophonist and composer, sometimes journalist you just mentioned. I really appreciate you coming today.
